definitions.name: Chow groups, refined intersections and Chern operations
definitions.define: Quotient dimension-graded cycles by rational equivalence, with proper pushforward, flat pullback, regular-immersion refined Gysin maps, Chern operators and their relations. Start with finite-type schemes over a field. Extend to the stated quotient-stratified algebraic stacks and rational proper-support Chow groups, retaining stabilizer denominators; compare degree and cycle-class operations only within their coefficient and smoothness hypotheses.

library.missing: The pin supplies locally finite cycles with a residue-degree-weighted pushforward (only map_id proved) and Weil divisors embedded in cycles. It also supplies principal divisors and the divisor class group of a Noetherian integral scheme, with an injection into line-bundle classes: rational equivalence in codimension one only. Missing: dimension-graded Chow groups (rational equivalence in all dimensions), pushforward descending to Chow groups, flat/lci pullback, Chern operators, refined Gysin maps and intersection products. The Edidin–Graham/Kresch extension to quotient-stratified stacks and proper-support rational Chow groups are also missing; they are unplanned scope in SF.5. SF.5 is the general supplier and SR4 owns the arithmetic-surface case. SchemeKTheoryOperations S.7 also plans Chern classes, excess intersection and deformation to the normal cone, which duplicates SF.5.

api.statement: CH*(P²_k)=Z[h]/(h³), and the degree of h² is 1.
CH₀(A¹_k)=0: the divisor of t on A¹ is [0]; on P¹ the principal divisor is [0]−[∞] and CH₀(P¹)=Z.
Two copies of a line in P² cannot be intersected by counting set-theoretic intersection points: the self-intersection class is a single point of degree 1.
For a constant finite group G of order n over an algebraically closed field, the rational stack degree of [BG] is 1/n, not 1.
For a closed immersion Z→X with open complement U, CH_i(Z)→CH_i(X)→CH_i(U)→0 is exact.
For a vector bundle E of rank r and its zero section s, the self-intersection operator s!s_* is c_r(E) cap −.
Proper pushforward and refined pullback satisfy projection and excess-intersection formulas, with codimension shifts and excess-bundle Chern class specified.

definitions.name: Flat torsors, contracted products and twisting
definitions.define: For a flat finitely presented group algebraic space G over S, define the groupoid of right G-torsors on the fppf site, locally equivariantly isomorphic to G. For arbitrary flat affine G use fpqc torsors without imposing finite presentation; compare this with the fppf formulation when G is finitely presented. Construct contracted products, associated bundles, inner forms and the pointed set of isomorphism classes H¹(S,G), without choosing a global point.

library.missing: Tau Ceti proves the torsor kernel-pair square for the fppf sheaf quotient of an affine group over a ring by a normal Hopf ideal (affine base, no representability). Mathlib has the fppf/fpqc topologies on schemes, fpqc descent of isomorphisms, set-level torsors and Čech nonabelian H¹ of a presheaf of groups for one fixed family (no colimit over covers, no comparison with torsor classes). Missing: the groupoid of G-torsors over a base scheme, H¹(S,G) as torsor classes, contracted products and associated bundles with their representability, inner forms and twisting. Finite torsors and descent come from ModularCurves 0C/0E; RP.3 is the arithmetic descent application.

api.statement: The trivial right G-torsor G→S has neutral H¹ class, and G ×^G V is isomorphic to V.
The frame torsor of O(1) on P¹ is a G_m-torsor with line-bundle class 1 in Pic(P¹)=Z.
In characteristic p, s↦s^p on G_m is a μ_p-torsor for the fppf topology and is not étale. Étale local triviality would omit this torsor.
A G-equivariant map between two G-torsors over S is an isomorphism, although a torsor need not have an S-section.
Contracted products commute with base change; twisting by a trivial torsor gives the original object.
Twisting by E identifies H¹(S,Aut_G(E)) with H¹(S,G), carrying the neutral class to [E].

The frame torsor of O(1) on P¹ has no global section, because O(1) has no nowhere-vanishing section. The empty scheme with the trivial G-action satisfies E×_S G≅E×_S E (both are empty) but is not a G-torsor over a nonempty S. The definition must require E→S to be an fppf covering, i.e. to have sections fppf-locally.

definitions.name: Normal-crossings boundaries and good compactifications
definitions.define: Define strict normal crossings by regular local parameters whose distinct product cuts out the reduced boundary, and normal crossings by étale-local strict normal crossings. For a smooth S-family define the relative version using relative coordinate hyperplanes. A good compactification is an open immersion into a smooth proper S-family with that boundary; projectivity and existence of such a model are separate conditions.

library.missing: Schemes and codimension-one cycles exist, but the local-coordinate boundary structure, its strata, relative charts and compactification interface are missing. R09.7a/7d cover characteristic zero; mixed-characteristic relative boundaries and arithmetic surface instances need an explicit extension of scope, not a claim of general resolution.

api.statement: The boundary xy=0 in A²_k is strict normal crossings, with two one-dimensional strata closures meeting at the origin in codimension two.
G_m⊂P¹ with boundary {0,∞} is a good smooth projective compactification.

The nodal cubic y²=x²(x+1) in A²_k (char k≠2) is normal crossings but not strict normal crossings (étale-locally uv=0 at the origin, but its only component is singular). Three concurrent lines xy(x+y)=0 in A²_k are not normal crossings although each component is regular and they meet pairwise transversally. The cusp y²=x³ is not normal crossings because its tangent cone is a double line.
The pullback of the reduced divisor t=0 on A¹ along t=s² is 2[0], not a reduced normal-crossings divisor. Arbitrary base change does not preserve the absolute condition.
Smooth pullback preserves absolute normal crossings; arbitrary base change preserves the relative chart condition for a smooth family.
For strict normal crossings, every nonempty intersection of r distinct components is regular of codimension r.

A smooth quasi-projective variety over a characteristic-zero field has a smooth projective compactification with strict normal-crossings boundary; do not export this existence statement in arbitrary characteristic.

definitions.name: Excellent rings and schemes (G-rings, J-2, universal catenarity)
definitions.define: For a Noetherian ring A: A is a G-ring if for every prime p the formal fibres of A_p → (A_p)^ are geometrically regular (a regular ring map: flat with geometrically regular fibres); A is J-2 if every finite-type A-algebra has open regular locus; A is universally catenary if every finite-type A-algebra is catenary. Quasi-excellent = G-ring + J-2; excellent = quasi-excellent + universally catenary. A locally Noetherian scheme is (quasi-)excellent if it has an open affine cover by spectra of (quasi-)excellent rings. Keep CESNAVICIUS-21's variants (CM- and (S_n)-quasi-excellence: formal fibres CM/(S_n) plus nonempty CM/(S_n) open on integral closed subschemes) as instances of the same template with the regularity condition replaced.

library.missing: No formal fibres, geometric regularity of ring maps, G-rings, J-2/openness of the regular locus, catenary or universally catenary rings, quasi-excellent or excellent rings/schemes at either pin. TauCeti/RingTheory/IntegralClosure/NormalizationFinite.lean (module docstring) records that the pinned Mathlib has no IsNagata/IsJapanese/IsExcellent; grep of both pinned trees for excellen/catenar finds no declaration.

api.statement: Every field, Z, every Dedekind domain whose fraction field has characteristic 0, and every complete Noetherian local ring is excellent; every finite-type algebra over an excellent ring is excellent.

Let k have characteristic p with [k:k^p] infinite and let R ⊂ k[[x]] be the DVR of power series whose coefficients generate a finite extension of k^p. R is regular and universally catenary but not excellent (not even Japanese): its generic formal fibre is not geometrically regular. A definition that keeps only Noetherian + regular/universally catenary wrongly accepts R.

Nagata's examples give Noetherian local domains that are not universally catenary (a 2-dimensional catenary local domain R with R[x] not catenary); these are Noetherian but not excellent, so 'locally Noetherian' cannot stand in for excellence in the consumers' hypotheses.
If X is quasi-excellent, the regular locus of every scheme locally of finite type over X is open (J-2).
For a reduced (resp. normal) excellent local ring R, the completion R^ is reduced (resp. normal); the normalization of a reduced excellent ring is finite over it.

(Quasi-)excellence passes to localizations, quotients and finite-type algebras, and is Zariski local: a locally Noetherian scheme is excellent iff some (equivalently every) affine open cover consists of spectra of excellent rings.
Every excellent scheme is CM-excellent and (S_n)-excellent for all n (regular formal fibres are CM and (S_n)), matching CESNAVICIUS-21 Definition 1.2 and §2.10.

definitions.name: Coarse moduli spaces of algebraic stacks
definitions.define: For an algebraic stack X define a coarse moduli map X→M to an algebraic space by its universal property for maps to algebraic spaces and its bijection on geometric isomorphism classes. Construct it in the finite-inertia Noetherian setting, keeping separatedness, tameness and base-change hypotheses explicit. It is not a fine moduli object.

library.missing: Generic stacks and schemes exist but no coarse-moduli-space structure, construction or stabilizer-sensitive comparison exists. ModularCurves9D owns its particular finite-quotient coarse schemes; it is imported rather than generalized without proof. Abelian-moduli applications alone do not construct the general finite-inertia supplier.

api.statement: The coarse moduli space of a scheme X is X with the identity map.
For a finite constant group G over an algebraically closed field, the coarse space of BG is Spec(k).
For nontrivial G the coarse point of BG does not classify its objects as a groupoid, since the trivial torsor has automorphisms G.
Two coarse moduli spaces satisfying the stated universal property are uniquely isomorphic compatibly with their maps.
For an affine scheme with finite group action, the coarse map of the quotient stack is given by the invariant-ring quotient under the usual finite-type hypotheses.

For tame X with finite inertia, coarse-space formation commutes with arbitrary base change S' → S. It fails in the non-tame case. Let G = Z/2 act on A¹_Z by x ↦ −x. The coarse space of [A¹_Z/G] is Spec Z[x²], with fibre Spec F₂[x²] over F₂. The fibre stack [A¹_{F₂}/G] has trivial action, so its coarse space is Spec F₂[x], and F₂[x²] → F₂[x] (Frobenius) is not an isomorphism.

sourceEvidence: GWZ20-B Situation2.6; Stacks0DUF and04UX; AOV08 Theorem3.2 and Corollary3.3 (source record in report).

definitions.name: Azumaya algebras and Brauer groups on schemes
definitions.define: Define finite locally free Azumaya O_X-algebras étale-locally matrix algebras, their Morita classes and tensor Brauer group. Construct the PGL_n torsor and boundary class in étale H²(G_m). Distinguish Azumaya Br, torsion cohomological Br′ and the ambient H²; define Br₀ and Br₁ only after specifying a ground field and geometric base change.

library.missing: IsAzumaya is a ring-algebra predicate, and MoritaEquivalence is ring-level. BrauerGroup is the field CSA quotient, which Tau Ceti makes a commutative group with base change and Br(ℝ)≅ℤ/2. None of these gives the sheaf-of-algebras (Azumaya O_X-algebra) carrier, Morita classes over a scheme, the PGL_n projective-frame torsor, or the boundary H¹(X,PGL_n)→H²_et(X,G_m) with the Br⊆Br′⊆H² comparison. H² itself is an existing specialization of Sheaf.H on the small étale site, and is not the claimed gap.

api.statement: For n≥1, End(O_X^n) is Azumaya and has Brauer class zero.
Over R, the quaternion algebra H has nonzero class of order two; after pullback to C it is split.
For a field k, k[ε]/ε² is finite free over k but not Azumaya: its nonzero proper nilpotent ideal prevents simplicity. Finite freeness alone is insufficient.
The opposite algebra represents the inverse Brauer class: A⊗A^op has zero class.
The PGL_n boundary sends a projective-frame torsor to its Azumaya Brauer class, with zero class exactly the split Morita class.
Pullback commutes with tensor products, opposite algebras and the cohomological boundary.
For a field k the sheaf definition agrees with the classical CSA Brauer group; equality Br=Br′ on more general schemes is a theorem with additional hypotheses, not a definition.

sourceEvidence: Cesnavicius–Scholze24 catalogue118; Cesnavicius19 cohom-brauer; Harpaz–Wittenberg20 catalogue14; pinned Azumaya and BrauerGroup definitions.

definitions.name: Algebraic quotient stacks and their atlases
definitions.define: For a smooth group algebraic space G acting on an S-algebraic space U, construct the fppf stack [U/G] whose objects over T are G-torsors P→T equipped with equivariant maps P→U. Retain morphisms, descent and stabilizers. Define algebraic and Deligne–Mumford stack conditions separately and compare general groupoid presentations.

library.missing: The generic IsStack class expresses effective descent but has no algebraic-stack carrier, representable diagonal, smooth atlas or quotient-stack construction. The fixed Hopf quotient sheaf in Tau Ceti is a sheaf of sets, not this stack. Profinite classifying gerbes need a further limit construction and are not asserted algebraic here.

api.statement: The quotient [U/1] is the stack represented by U, with trivial automorphism groups.
For a finite constant nontrivial G over an algebraically closed field, BG has one isomorphism class of geometric objects and automorphism group G.
BG is not equivalent to its coarse point when G is nontrivial: replacing the stack by the orbit set loses its automorphisms.
For smooth G, the map U→[U/G] is a representable smooth surjection; pulling it back to (P→T,P→U) recovers P→T.
The construction commutes with base change and with equivariant isomorphisms of the action data.
If P→X is a G-torsor, the quotient stack [P/G] is equivalent to X, with the torsor kernel-pair square as its atlas relation.

Over R, [Spec R/(Z/2)](R) has two isomorphism classes (Spec R⊔Spec R and Spec C, since H¹(R,Z/2)={±1}). The unstackified action groupoid has one object over Spec R, so omitting fppf stackification fails.

sourceEvidence: GWZ20 arXiv1707.06417, §2.1; Stacks 06PA and 06PD; EVW16 catalogue supplier126; GWZ20-B catalogue87 for smooth group-space actions.

definitions.name: Coherent dualizing complexes and exceptional inverse image
definitions.define: For separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base construct coherent f! on bounded-below quasicoherent derived categories, with its composition constraints. For proper f it is the right adjoint of Rf*. Define dualizing complexes affine-locally by bounded coherent cohomology, finite injective dimension and the biduality condition, with normalization pinned. Include finite traces and lci determinant/fundamental-class comparisons.

library.missing: Ordinary derived categories and cohomology exist, not coherent f!, normalized dualizing complexes, trace/counit or their comparison with the cotangent determinant. StableReduction2 supplies curve duality only. EDC.1 is étale Verdier duality with different coefficients and is not the coherent supplier; EnhancedDerivedSheaves supplies enhancements, not this geometric duality theory. Review note: the draft roadmap AnalyticStacks (research/blueprint/roadmaps/AnalyticStacks.json) plans, at AS.3, the solid quasi-coherent six functors, including f^!1 ≅ det L for lci maps and Serre duality for P¹_Z. That is a partial supplier for the analytic/solid branch; scheme-theoretic coherent f^! on Noetherian schemes is still unplanned. Nagata compactification (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2) is a prerequisite of the general construction.

api.statement: For P¹_k→Spec(k), f!k=O(−2)[1], using cohomological shifts.
For Spec(F_p)→Spec(Z), f!Z=F_p[−1]: its only nonzero cohomology is H¹=F_p.
Ordinary Hom_Z(F_p,Z)=0, so replacing the derived finite-map formula by ordinary Hom loses the preceding nonzero example.
For a finite map f, f_*f!M is RHom(f_*O_X,M); for a finite flat map and M=O this reduces to the algebra dual in degree zero.

A Noetherian local ring with normalized dualizing complex ω• is Cohen–Macaulay iff ω• has exactly one nonzero cohomology module (in degree −dim A). For A=k[x,y]_{(x,y)}/(x²,xy) (dimension 1, depth 0), both H^{−1}(ω•) and H^0(ω•)≅H^0_m(A)^∨ are nonzero, so a definition keeping only the canonical module H^{−d}(ω•) loses information.
For composable separated finite-type maps, (gf)! identifies coherently with f!g!; proper trace maps are the adjunction counits and compose accordingly.
For k[ε]/ε² over a characteristic-zero field, the algebra trace kills ε and the trace pairing is degenerate. The finite-flat fundamental class is not automatically an isomorphism O_X→f!O_Y.

sourceEvidence: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AU3, properties1–9; Bhatt et al23 §2.1 PDF9–10; Pilloni20 §4.1.3 and §4.2.2 catalogue statements.

definitions.name: Perfect schemes and spaces with finite-presentation models
definitions.define: For an F_p-scheme or algebraic space construct its inverse limit along absolute Frobenius, with the k-Frobenius twists when working over a general perfect field k. Affinely the coordinate ring is the direct-limit perfect closure. Define perfectly finite presentation by étale-local finite-presentation models, and perfectly proper and smooth morphisms through deperfections, independently of the chosen models.

library.missing: PerfectClosure already constructs the direct-limit perfect closure of any commutative characteristic-p ring, while Perfection is the inverse-limit power-map construction. Missing are geometric gluing/algebraic-space descent, the geometric adjunction, pfp models and their morphism API. The entry must reuse PerfectClosure on affines, not claim that ring construction is absent.

api.statement: The perfection of Spec(F_p[t]) is Spec(F_p[t^(1/p^∞)]), whereas the perfection of Spec(F_p) is itself.
The perfection of Spec(k[ε]/ε²) for perfect k is Spec(k), since a sufficiently high Frobenius kills ε.
Perfect affine one-space is perfectly finitely presented but is not of finite type over k; replacing pfp by ordinary finite presentation is wrong.
For a perfect algebraic space Y, composition with X^perf→X gives Hom(Y,X^perf)≅Hom(Y,X).
Geometric perfection commutes with finite limits, and its projection induces an equivalence of small étale topoi.

A pfp perfect algebraic space admits a finite-presentation deperfection, but the model is not unique: A¹ and the cuspidal cubic Spec k[t²,t³] are non-isomorphic finite-type models with isomorphic perfections.

Using the inverse-limit ring Perfection on coordinate rings is wrong: for A=F_p[t], Perfection(A)=F_p (only constants have compatible p-power roots), so Spec(Perfection A)=Spec F_p, whereas (A¹_{F_p})^perf=Spec F_p[t^{1/p^∞}]=Spec(PerfectClosure A).

sourceEvidence: Zhu17 published Appendix A.1.1–A.1.2 pp.464–466 and A.2.1 pp.471–472 (PDF62–64,69–70).

definitions.name: Sheaf cohomology with closed supports and localization
definitions.define: On the specified ringed space or scheme site with a closed support Z and open complement U, construct derived sections with support, its local sheaf version, restriction maps and localization triangle. Compare the right-derived support functor with the fibre of RΓ(X,−)→RΓ(U,−); distinguish closed supports from compact support and arbitrary families of supports.

library.missing: The pin has ordinary derived categories and Ext-defined sheaf cohomology. It lacks this functorial derived support/restriction comparison, local support sheaves and excision API. The fibre formula alone is not the missing object: constructing RΓ and its localization maps on the actual coefficient categories is the work. EDC.0 and upstream point-counting supply their finite constructible cases; SF.2 retains site/coefficient comparisons beyond those cases.

api.statement: For the empty support RΓ_∅(X,F)=0, whereas full support gives RΓ_X(X,F)=RΓ(X,F).
For X=Spec(k[t]), Z=V(t), and F=O_X, H¹_Z(X,F)=k[t,t⁻¹]/k[t], while H⁰_Z(X,F)=0.

In the affine-line example H⁰_Z(X,O_X)=0 and H¹_Z(X,O_X)=k[t,t⁻¹]/k[t]≠0, whereas cohomology of the restriction gives H⁰(Z,i^{-1}O_X)=O_{X,0}≠0 and H⁰(Z,O_Z)=k≠0. Neither restriction nor underived supported sections computes RΓ_Z.
RΓ_Z(X,F)→RΓ(X,F)→RΓ(U,F|U) is a distinguished triangle inducing the localization long exact sequence.
An open neighbourhood V of Z gives an excision isomorphism RΓ_Z(X,F)≅RΓ_Z(V,F|V).
For Z⊂Y closed, the nested-support triangle relates RΓ_Z(X,F), RΓ_Y(X,F), and RΓ_(Y−Z)(X−Z,F).

sourceEvidence: Cesnavicius22 Lemma7.2(a); Bhatt et al23 PDF10 equation(2.1.1); Benoist–Wittenberg20 support-theory catalogue supplier; Kings–Sprang25 AppendixA DefinitionA.3 for the equivariant extension.

definitions.name: Numerical divisor and curve spaces, nef cones and numerical Picard
definitions.define: For a projective morphism in the Noetherian source setting form real Cartier-divisor and contracted-curve spaces modulo the degree pairing, retaining the rational structure. Define N¹, N₁, the closed effective cone and its nef dual. For a proper scheme over a field, separately construct Pic^τ and the quotient étale numerical Picard sheaf; compare its geometric lattice with numerical divisor classes under the source hypotheses.

library.missing: Line bundles, their iso-class group (LineBundleClass), Weil divisors with residue-weighted curve degree, cycles with proper pushforward, and a generic 'quotient by the radicals of a pairing' with its nondegenerate descended pairing (TauCeti.numericalPairing) exist. Missing: the degree of a line bundle on a proper integral curve in X, the degree pairing Pic(X)⊗R × Z₁(X/S)_R → R that the numerical quotient would be applied to, finite-dimensionality of N¹, the closed effective curve cone and the nef cone, and the Picard sheaf with its Pic^τ subsheaf and étale quotient Num. MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.0 plans absolute numerical equivalence of cycles on smooth projective varieties only; the relative, cone and Pic^τ parts are unplanned.

api.statement: For n≥1, N¹(P^n/k) is R generated by O(1); its nef cone is R≥0 and the degree of O(a) on a line is a.
On P¹×P¹ the two ruling classes have squares zero and mutual intersection one; O(a,b) is nef exactly when a,b≥0.
A nontrivial degree-zero line bundle on a smooth projective elliptic curve is numerically trivial without being trivial in Pic. Numerical equivalence is coarser than linear equivalence.
O(−1) on P² has top self-intersection 1 and no positive-power sections, so it is not big. Positivity of the top intersection characterizes bigness only with the required nef hypothesis.

For X projective over a field, N¹(X)_R is finite-dimensional. (Kleiman) A Cartier divisor D is ample iff D·z>0 for all z ∈ NE-bar(X)∖{0}, and the nef cone is the closure of the ample cone. The closure is needed: Mumford's ruled surface over a curve of genus ≥2 carries a divisor positive on every curve with D²=0, which is not ample.
Proper pushforward of contracted curves and pullback of Cartier divisors satisfy the degree projection formula wherever these operations are defined.
In the proper-field source setting the geometric fibre of Pic/Pic^τ is a finite-rank free abelian group, with its Galois action retained.

sourceEvidence: Bhatt–Ma–Patakfalvi–Schwede–Tucker–Waldron–Witaszek23 §2.5, PDF18–19; Schröer23 catalogue Definition1; Bhatt–Scholze17 G811 is read with the nef qualification, not as positive self-intersection alone.

definitions.name: Algebraic spaces and representable morphisms
definitions.define: Define an étale sheaf of sets on schemes whose diagonal is representable by schemes and which admits a surjective étale atlas by a scheme. Construct morphisms, fibre products and the small étale site independently of an atlas. Do not impose quasi-separatedness unless the application requests it.

library.missing: Mathlib has schemes, the big and small étale topologies, representable and P-representable morphisms of presheaves with base-change stability and the representable-diagonal lemma, and Zariski-local representability. So the carrier (an étale sheaf with representable diagonal and an étale surjective scheme atlas) is a short structure over existing API. Missing: the carrier itself and its substance. That is the theorem that the sheaf quotient of an étale equivalence relation of schemes is an algebraic space with R = U ×_{U/R} U, properties of morphisms of spaces defined étale-locally, the small étale site of a space and its descent comparison with an atlas, and quasi-coherent sheaves on spaces. Spectral E₂-spaces remain excluded.

api.statement: Over the base S = Spec k, the algebraic space h_{Spec k} is the final object, with exactly one T-point for every k-scheme T. More generally, X ↦ h_X is fully faithful from S-schemes to algebraic spaces over S.
For the translation action of Z/2 on two disjoint copies of Spec(k), the étale sheaf quotient is Spec(k).
The affine line with doubled origin is a scheme, hence an algebraic space, but is not separated. Requiring a closed diagonal in the definition would reject it.
An étale equivalence relation R ⇉ U of schemes has an algebraic-space sheaf quotient, with R identified with U ×_(U/R) U.
For any étale atlas U → X with R = U ×_X U, restriction gives an equivalence between sheaves on X_et and sheaves on U_et with descent data along R ⇉ U. The same holds for quasi-coherent O_X-modules.

Algebraic spaces have fibre products, computed as fibre products of sheaves, and a morphism from a scheme to an algebraic space is representable by algebraic spaces. The second follows from the representable diagonal (Mathlib's relativelyRepresentable.of_diag once the carrier exists). Also: every quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space contains a dense open subspace that is a scheme.

sourceEvidence: Zhu17, published Appendix A.1.1, pp.464–465 (PDF62–63).

definitions.name: Hilbert and Quot functors with universal families
definitions.define: For X→S projective of finite presentation and a finitely presented quasicoherent sheaf E, define the Quot functor of finitely presented quotients E_T→F flat over T, modulo isomorphism of quotients, with a fixed Hilbert polynomial. Hilbert is the E=O_X case. Construct representing schemes and their universal quotients under the stated Noetherian hypotheses.

library.missing: The module Grassmannian already parameterizes submodules with finite projective fixed-rank quotient. Its own TODO records that scheme charts and representability are absent; those belong to ModularCurves0G. The general Hilbert/Quot functor, flat families, universal quotient and representability are additional work, not the finite-source Hom functor owned by 0F.

api.statement: For a field k, Quot of k^r with quotient dimension d is the Grassmannian of d-dimensional quotients; d=0 gives Spec(k).
Hilb¹ of a separated k-scheme X is X, with universal family the diagonal.
The quotient k[t]→k[t]/(t), viewed over Spec(k[t]), is not a Hilbert family: its fibre length jumps from zero to one and it is not flat.
Hilbert is naturally isomorphic to Quot of the structure sheaf by sending a closed family to its structure-sheaf quotient.

Hilb^n(P¹_k) ≅ P^n_k (effective divisors of degree n are binary forms of degree n up to scalar), and Hilb^P → S is proper. For example, the family {0,t} ⊂ A¹ over A¹∖{0} has the double point V(x²) as its unique flat limit at t=0, whereas the reduced limit {0} has the wrong Hilbert polynomial.
At a quotient E→F on a projective k-scheme, the Zariski tangent space is Hom(ker(E→F),F).

definitions.name: Moduli stacks of smooth and stable pointed curves
definitions.define: For 2g−2+n>0 construct M_(g,n) and its stable compactification as groupoid-valued moduli of proper flat connected genus-g curves with n disjoint smooth sections, using the upstream stable-curve definition and ampleness of ω(sum sections). Construct universal families, forgetful maps with stabilization and clutching maps. Keep the stack, its coarse space and a fine level cover distinct.

library.missing: Generic schemes/stacks and line bundles do not construct these moduli stacks or their universal families. StableReduction supplies the stable curves, marked stabilization and valuative reduction, explicitly not the moduli stack. The proposed MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves roadmap is not an accepted stage; R09.4 currently lists elliptic/abelian examples without this full supplier.

api.statement: M_(0,3)=Spec(k): every ordered triple of distinct points on P¹ has a unique projective coordinate sending it to 0,1,∞.
M_(0,4)=P¹−{0,1,∞}, via cross-ratio, and its stable compactification is P¹.
A smooth elliptic curve with its origin in characteristic zero has the nonidentity automorphism [−1]. Its coarse moduli point cannot be a fine representative of the moduli groupoid.
The stable pointed moduli stack is proper and Deligne–Mumford, with relative dimension 3g−3+n; the smooth-curve locus is open.

(Knudsen) The universal curve C̄_{g,n} → M̄_{g,n} is isomorphic to the forgetful-and-stabilize map M̄_{g,n+1} → M̄_{g,n}, compatibly with the n sections. In particular M̄_{0,4} → M̄_{0,3} = Spec k is the universal curve P¹ over a point.
Forgetting a marking followed by stabilization defines the moduli morphism whenever the resulting (g,n−1) remains stable; an unstable rational tail is contracted.

definitions.name: Weil restriction beyond affine targets
definitions.define: For a finite locally free map S′→S and an algebraic space X/S′, construct the S-space representing T↦Hom_(S′)(T×_S S′,X). Import affine-target Weil restriction from ModularCurves0F. Prove the space construction by descent, scheme representability in the quasi-projective cases used here, and the finite-étale preservation results separately.

library.missing: The pins have schemes and categorical descent but no general representable Weil-restriction space. The upstream affine package does not cover projective flags or abelian varieties; accepted RS-27 assigns precisely this residual generality to R09.3.

api.statement: Res_(C/R)(A¹_C)=A²_R, with z=a+bi corresponding to (a,b); this must agree with the imported affine construction.
For the split quadratic cover Spec(k×k)→Spec(k), restriction of a pair (X₁,X₂) is X₁×X₂; in particular (P¹,P¹) gives P¹×P¹.

Along Spec(k[ε]/ε²)→Spec(k), restriction of P¹ over the dual numbers is the tangent bundle T(P¹), which is not proper. Finite locally free is insufficient for preservation of properness; the finite-étale hypothesis matters.
The representing space satisfies Hom_S(T,Res X)=Hom_(S′)(T×_S S′,X), naturally in T and X.
Formation of Weil restriction commutes with arbitrary base change on S.

For finite locally free S′→S, Res_{S′/S} preserves smoothness. For finite étale S′→S it also preserves properness, because étale-locally on S the restriction is a finite product; the dual-numbers example shows that properness fails without étaleness.

definitions.name: Gerbes, abelian bandings and neutralizations
definitions.define: On a specified étale or fppf site define a gerbe as a stack in groupoids that is locally nonempty and whose objects are locally isomorphic. Define an A-banding for an abelian sheaf A with pullback and conjugation compatibility, morphisms preserving the band, and neutralizations. Construct profinite étale gerbes as cofiltered 2-limits of finite étale gerbes on the fpqc site, with compatible objects and transition isomorphisms. Keep this limit construction distinct from an algebraic stack of finite presentation.

library.missing: IsStack and abelian sheaf cohomology exist, but gerbe/band/neutralization data, their 2-morphisms and the H² classification do not. The finite and general site constructions extend to compatible fpqc 2-limits; the limit universal property and change of topology are work, with no algebraicity claim for the pro-object. Derived H² is not unconditionally replaced by Čech H².

api.statement: BA for an abelian sheaf A is a neutral A-gerbe, and its cohomology class is zero in H²(S,A).
Over an algebraically closed field with n invertible, the gerbe of nth roots of O(1) on P¹ has class δ(O(1)) and no global object when n>1.
A gerbe can be locally nonempty without being neutral: for n≥2 invertible in an algebraically closed k, the μ_n-gerbe of n-th roots of O(1) on P¹ has no global object, since O(1) has degree 1.
For an abelian band on the chosen site, equivalence classes of banded gerbes correspond to derived H²; the zero class is exactly the neutral class.
Pullback preserves bandings and carries the class of a gerbe to the pullback cohomology class.
Band-preserving self-equivalences of a neutral A-gerbe form the groupoid of A-torsors, including their isomorphisms.
An object of a cofiltered 2-limit gerbe over T consists of finite-stage objects together with compatible transition isomorphisms, not just a sequence of isomorphism classes.
The fpqc classifying gerbe of the constant profinite group Z_hat is not an algebraic stack of finite presentation: its stabilizer is not of finite type.

definitions.name: Henselization of pairs and of local rings
definitions.define: For a pair (R, I), its henselization (R^h, I^h) is the initial henselian pair under (R, I): R^h = colim of étale R-algebras S with R/I ≅ S/IS, I^h = IR^h. For a local ring (R, m) this is the henselization R^h; for a point x of a scheme, O^h_{X,x}. Keep the strict henselization (separably closed residue field, depending on a geometric point) as a separate, Tau Ceti-owned variant.

library.missing: Only the henselian-pair predicate exists; no henselization of a pair or of a local ring (grep of the pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti for henseliz/henselis finds nothing), and no ind-étale presentation or universal property.

api.statement: (R^h, IR^h) is henselian, R → R^h is a filtered colimit of étale maps with R/I ≅ R^h/IR^h, and every map from (R, I) to a henselian pair factors uniquely through R^h.
If (R, I) is already henselian (for instance R Noetherian and I-adically complete) then R^h = R.

The henselization of Z_(p) is the ring of p-adic integers algebraic over Q, a countable ring; it is not Z_p, so a definition by completion is wrong. Likewise k[x]_(x)^h consists of the power series algebraic over k(x) and omits e^x when char k = 0.
The henselization keeps the residue field: Z_(p)^h has residue field F_p, whereas the strict henselization has residue field a separable closure of F_p; the two constructions must not be conflated.
For a Noetherian local ring R, R^h is Noetherian local, R → R^h is faithfully flat, mR^h is the maximal ideal and (R^h)^ ≅ R^.
For an integral R-algebra S, the henselization of (S, IS) is S ⊗_R R^h; in particular (R/J)^h = R^h/JR^h.

definitions.name: Geometric quotients by group actions and finite equivalence relations
definitions.define: For a flat group scheme G of finite type over S acting on an S-scheme or algebraic space X, a G-invariant morphism π: X → Y is a geometric quotient if it is surjective and submersive (universally in the universal version), its geometric fibres are exactly the orbits, and O_Y → (π_*O_X)^G is an isomorphism; categorical and good quotients are the weaker variants. Include WITASZEK-22's geometric quotients of finite set-theoretic equivalence relations (finite coequalizers whose geometric fibres are the equivalence classes).

library.missing: Invariant subalgebras for group actions on rings exist, but not group-scheme actions on schemes with the invariant subsheaf (π_*O_X)^G, nor geometric/categorical/good quotients or quotients by finite equivalence relations.

api.statement: A finite group G acting on Spec A: Spec A → Spec A^G is a geometric quotient; it is integral and surjective, and its geometric fibres are single G-orbits.

G_m acting on A^2 by scaling: Spec k[x,y] → Spec k[x,y]^{G_m} = Spec k is a categorical quotient but not a geometric one (its one fibre contains infinitely many orbits); on A^2 ∖ {0} the geometric quotient is P^1.
G_m acting on A^1 by scaling has no geometric quotient in schemes: the orbits {0} and A^1 ∖ {0} are not separated while the invariants are only k.
A geometric quotient is a categorical quotient (Mumford, GIT Prop. 0.1); for a finite group acting on a quasi-projective scheme over a Noetherian base the geometric quotient exists.
For a finite group, forming the quotient commutes with flat base change Y' → Y, because invariants are a kernel and flat tensor products preserve kernels.

(Seshadri) For a reductive group scheme G over a Noetherian base acting on an affine X = Spec B of finite type, B^G is of finite type and X → Spec B^G is a good categorical quotient, geometric on the stable locus (BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/001).

definitions.name: Equivariant sheaves and derived invariant sections
definitions.define: For a discrete group Γ acting on a ringed space or site, construct the abelian category of sheaves with compatible pullback linearizations, and derive Γ-invariant global sections. Include equivariant Ext and invariant closed supports. A sheaf automorphism on a fixed base is insufficient when the group moves the base; continuous profinite actions are a separate extension.

library.missing: Action bundles automorphisms of a fixed categorical object, and groupCohomology supplies the point case. Missing are semilinear descent along the base action, enough-injectives/acyclicity comparisons and the composite-derived-functor spectral sequence for these sheaves. SF.2 does not explicitly own this arbitrary discrete-group ringed-space extension; finite-group actions in étale suppliers do not cover Kings–Sprang’s lattice action.

api.statement: For X a point, equivariant cohomology is group cohomology; for Γ=1 it is ordinary sheaf cohomology.
For Γ=C₂ acting trivially on Z at a point, H²_Γ(X,Z)=Z/2 and H¹_Γ(X,Z)=0.
In the preceding point example ordinary H²(X,Z)=0, so taking Γ-invariants only after ordinary cohomology would incorrectly give zero.
There is a spectral sequence H^p(Γ,H^q(X,F))⇒H^(p+q)_Γ(X,F) in the bounded-below setting with the required acyclicity comparison proved.
For a Γ-stable closed subset, restriction and the support inclusion produce an equivariant localization triangle.
For finite Γ whose order is invertible in the coefficient ring, invariants are exact and the spectral sequence collapses to H^n_Γ(X,F)=H^n(X,F)^Γ.
For Γ=ℤ acting on ℝ by translation and F=ℤ, H¹_Γ(ℝ,ℤ)=H¹(S¹,ℤ)=ℤ, while H¹(ℝ,ℤ)^Γ=0; a definition that ignores the base action or takes invariants after cohomology fails.

definitions.name: Galois gerbs with algebraic kernels and projective limits
definitions.define: For a characteristic-zero Galois extension k′/k define a topological extension of Gal(k′/k) by H(k′), with H a linear algebraic group and its point kernel discrete. Require algebraic semilinear conjugation and a continuous splitting over an open Galois subgroup that gives algebraic descent and a semidirect-product chart. Define morphisms continuous over Galois and algebraic on kernels, their conjugator schemes, and compatible projective systems for proalgebraic kernels. Do not replace stagewise conjugacy of pro-morphisms by an unproved single global conjugator.

library.missing: Generic actions and stacks do not provide the algebraic-kernel/topological-extension compatibility, descent charts, conjugator scheme or pro-gerb comparison. Kisin’s finite algebraic-kernel gerbs and the Kottwitz protorus gerbe in HKW22 instantiate the finite-stage/projective-system construction. BG1 plans B(G) invariants but not this Galois-gerb carrier; no accepted stage explicitly owns it.

api.statement: For H/k the neutral gerb is H(k′)⋊Gal(k′/k), with the identity Galois splitting and the original k-descent datum.
Over an algebraically closed field the Galois quotient is trivial and the neutral G_m gerb has algebraic kernel endomorphisms z↦z^n for integers n.

Over C/R the abstract automorphism (z,σ)↦(conjugate(z),σ) of the neutral G_m extension is continuous for the discrete kernel but is not algebraic over C on the kernel. Continuity alone does not define a gerb morphism.
The extension 1→μ₂(C)→C₄→Gal(C/R)=C₂→1 satisfies the finite-extension local splitting condition but has no global group-theoretic splitting: every lift of the generator has order four.
For a morphism f into the neutral gerb of G, its descended automorphism group becomes the centralizer of the algebraic kernel image after extension to k′.
Enlarging the Galois splitting field uses pullback on the Galois quotient and pushout on kernel points, retaining the algebraic maps.

For the Kottwitz gerbe ℰ of a p-adic field F, whose kernel is the protorus D with X*(D)=Q, algebraic kernel maps D→G_m are exactly the characters in X*(D)=Q. Each factors through a finite stage D_n with X*(D_n)=(1/n)Z. For G=GL₂ the basic class of slope 1/2 in B(GL₂) is realised by an algebraic cocycle of ℰ. Treating D as a single finite-type torus with character group Z would miss this class and break H¹_alg(ℰ,G(F̄)) ≅ B(G).

definitions.name: Inertia and relative automorphism groups
definitions.define: Define ordinary inertia of an algebraic stack X as the 2-fibre product of its diagonal with itself. Its objects are pairs (x,a) with a an automorphism of x. For X→Y define relative inertia using automorphisms that induce the identity in Y. Do not identify ordinary inertia with cyclotomic Hom(Bμ_n,X).

library.missing: Generic categorical isomorphisms and descent exist, but the algebraic inertia stack, relative inertia group space and quotient presentation do not. A pointwise automorphism type alone omits sheaf descent and the algebraic family.

api.statement: For a scheme X regarded as a stack, I_X is X: every geometric object has the trivial automorphism group.
For a constant finite group G, I_BG is [G/G] for conjugation; if G is abelian this is a disjoint union of |G| copies of BG.
For G=S₃ over an algebraically closed field, I_BG has three components, indexed by conjugacy classes, rather than six components indexed by group elements.
For a finite constant group acting on U, I_[U/G] is the disjoint union of [U^g/C_G(g)] over conjugacy classes.
Formation of relative inertia commutes with base change on the target stack.
For a morphism of Deligne–Mumford stacks, representability is equivalent to trivial vertical stabilizers at geometric points.

definitions.name: Relative spectrum and vector schemes
definitions.define: For a quasicoherent commutative O_X-algebra A construct Spec_X(A), representing O_T-algebra maps f*A→O_T over X. Glue affine spectra and prove independence of cover. Extend by étale descent to algebraic-space bases. Pin V(E)=Spec Sym(E), which represents linear functionals, and W(E)=V(E∨), which represents sections when E is finite locally free.

library.missing: Mathlib glues a quasi-coherent O_X-algebra into a scheme over X when the algebra is given as a coequifibered presheaf of rings on affine opens: AffineZariskiSite.relativeGluingData(...).glued, with coequifibered ⇔ localisation proved. Over an affine base, algSpec is fully faithful. Missing: (1) the category of quasi-coherent sheaves of O_X-algebras and its comparison with coequifibered presheaves; (2) the representing property Hom_X(T,Spec_X A)≅Hom_{O_T-alg}(f*A,O_T); (3) contravariant functoriality and the anti-equivalence with affine X-schemes; (4) base change; (5) Sym of a quasi-coherent module and V(E), W(E); (6) extension to algebraic-space bases.

api.statement: Spec_X(O_X)=X; Spec_X(O_X[t]) is the relative affine line.
For X=Spec(R) and A the sheaf of an R-algebra B, Spec_X(A)=Spec(B) over Spec(R).
On P¹, V(O(1)) has only its zero section since Hom(O(1),O)=0, whereas W(O(1)) has the two-dimensional k-vector space of sections. Interchanging E and E∨ reverses the convention.
The represented morphisms satisfy Hom_X(T,Spec_X A) ≅ Hom_(O_T-alg)(f*A,O_T), naturally in both arguments.
For any morphism g:X′→X, Spec_{X′}(g*A) identifies with X′×_X Spec_X A.
Relative spectrum is contravariant in A and gives an anti-equivalence between quasicoherent O_X-algebras and affine X-schemes.

definitions.name: Integrable Higgs bundles and parameter connections
definitions.define: Over a ringed space with differential forms, define finite locally free E with a λ-connection D satisfying D(ae)=aD(e)+λe⊗da, where λ is central and dλ=0, and impose integrability D²=0. At λ=0 this is a Higgs field θ with θ∧θ=0. Construct tensor, dual, twists, Griffiths filtrations and their associated graded Higgs objects.

library.missing: The pin has universal ring derivations and scheme line bundles, but no finite-locally-free Higgs/connection category, extended differential, curvature or filtered Rees construction. ET.2b owns its curve Hitchin application; the proposed HodgeStructuresPartII general ringed-site/higher-dimensional supplier has no stage in the atlas yet.

api.statement: On A¹_k, (O,d) is a rank-one flat connection; with λ=0, θ=dx is a rank-one integrable Higgs field.
For a constant λ, D=λd on O has curvature zero; λ=1 and λ=0 recover the ordinary differential and zero Higgs field.
On A²_k the field E12 dx+E21 dy on O² is not integrable: its exterior square is [E12,E21] dx∧dy, which is nonzero.
The rank-one Higgs field dx on A¹ is integrable and not tensor-nilpotent. Exterior-square integrability cannot replace a nilpotence condition.
If λ is invertible and dλ=0, λ⁻¹D is an ordinary integrable connection.
Tensor products of two λ-connections (same λ) use D_E⊗1+1⊗D_F and are again λ-connections, not 2λ-connections. Duals and pullbacks preserve the Leibniz rule and integrability.
A Griffiths-transverse filtration on a flat bundle induces an integrable Higgs field on its associated graded.

definitions.name: Witt-vector structure sheaves W_n O_X and Witt schemes W_n(X)
definitions.define: For a scheme X on which p is locally nilpotent, W_n O_X is the sheaf U ↦ W_n(O_X(U)) of p-typical length-n Witt vectors on |X|, and W_n(X) = (|X|, W_n O_X), a scheme with W_n(Spec A) = Spec W_n(A); W O_X = lim_n W_n O_X and, for X perfect, W(X) = colim_n W_n(X) is a p-adic formal scheme. Record restriction R, Frobenius F and Verschiebung V as maps of sheaves/schemes.

library.missing: Ring-level Witt vectors exist, but not the localization isomorphism W_n(A_f) ≅ W_n(A)_[f], the sheaf W_n O_X, the scheme W_n(X) or the formal scheme W(X); no file of Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector mentions localization.

api.statement: W_1(X) = X and W_n(Spec A) = Spec W_n(A); when p is nilpotent on A, W_n(A) → A has nilpotent kernel, so |W_n(X)| = |X|.
For A = Q (p invertible) the ghost map gives W_n(Q) ≅ Q^n, so Spec W_n(Q) has n points: the 'same underlying space' statement needs p locally nilpotent.
For f ∈ A, W_n(A_f) ≅ W_n(A)[1/[f]] (localization at the Teichmüller lift), so U ↦ W_n(O_X(U)) is a sheaf and the affine pieces glue to the scheme W_n(X).
If A → B is étale then W_n(A) → W_n(B) is étale, so W_n commutes with étale localization and W_n O_X is an étale sheaf.
For X perfect over F_p, W_n(X) is flat over Z/p^n with W_n(X) ×_{Z/p^n} F_p ≅ X, and W(X) is a p-adic formal scheme flat over Z_p (BHATT-SCHOLZE-17 §4).
For A = F_p[x], W_2(A) is not flat over Z/p^2: p·(a_0,a_1) = (0, a_0^p), so (0, x) is p-torsion but not in p·W_2(A). The flatness/lifting statement requires perfectness.
Restriction W_{n+1}(A) → W_n(A) is surjective, making W_n(X) a closed subscheme of W_{n+1}(X); F and V are compatible with R, and F is an automorphism when X is perfect.

definitions.name: Root stacks of line bundles with sections and of Cartier divisors
definitions.define: For a scheme (or stack) X, a line bundle L with section s and n ≥ 1, the n-th root stack X_{(L,s),n} is the fibre product X ×_{[A^1/G_m]} [A^1/G_m] along the n-th power map; its T-objects are (M, t, φ: M^{⊗n} ≅ L_T) with φ(t^n) = s_T. For an effective Cartier divisor D take (O(D), s_D). Include the relative version along a closed subscheme R used by YUN-ZHANG-19 (square roots of L|_R with a root of s|_R, i.e. the pullback of the squaring map on [Res_R A^1 / Res_R G_m]), and the infinite root stack lim_n as in BRESCIANI-24/37.

library.missing: No algebraic stacks, quotient stacks [A^1/G_m] or μ_n-quotients, and no root-stack construction at either pin; only the abstract descent/stack condition for pseudofunctors exists.

api.statement: For X = Spec R and D = V(f) with f a nonzerodivisor, the n-th root stack is [Spec R[t]/(t^n − f) / μ_n] with ζ·t = ζt (BRESCIANI-24/36 for a DVR and its uniformizer).
The map X_{(L,s),n} → X is a coarse moduli space and an isomorphism over X ∖ V(s); affinely (R[t]/(t^n − f))^{μ_n} = R.
Over a point x ∈ V(s) the fibre is [Spec k[t]/(t^n)/μ_n], which is non-reduced; only its reduction is Bμ_n. Replacing the fibre by Bμ_n is wrong (YUN-ZHANG-19/160 records this for n = 2).

If X is regular, V(s) a regular divisor and n invertible on X, the root stack is a regular Deligne–Mumford stack; if char k = p divides n, the stabilizer μ_n is not étale and the root stack is an Artin stack that is not Deligne–Mumford, so the invertibility hypothesis matters.
For f: Y → X, Y_{f^*(L,s),n} ≅ Y ×_X X_{(L,s),n}; for m ≥ 1, (M, t) ↦ (M^{⊗m}, t^m) gives X_{(L,s),mn} → X_{(L,s),n}, and the infinite root stack is the limit of this system.
For a DVR R with residue field k, the reduced closed fibre of the infinite root stack of Spec R is (noncanonically) B_k Ẑ(1), and its k-points up to isomorphism are H^1(k, Ẑ(1)) (BRESCIANI-24/37).

definitions.name: Étale K(π,1) schemes
definitions.define: A connected, geometrically pointed, locally Noetherian scheme (X, x̄) is an étale K(π,1) for a class C of finite coefficients if for every finite discrete π_1^ét(X, x̄)-module F in C the edge maps H^i(π_1^ét(X, x̄), F) → H^i_ét(X, F) are isomorphisms for all i. Full version: all finite coefficients (equivalently π_n^ét(X, x̄) = 0 for n ≥ 2, Artin–Mazur); FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 uses the p-power-order version. The coefficient class is part of the data.

library.missing: Galois categories, fundamental groups of fibre functors and the étale precoverage exist, but there is no étale cohomology of schemes, no comparison map from continuous group cohomology of π_1^ét, and no étale homotopy type.

api.statement: Spec k of a field is an étale K(π,1) for all finite coefficients: étale cohomology of Spec k is Galois cohomology of G_k = π_1^ét(Spec k).

P^1 over an algebraically closed field is not a K(π,1): π_1^ét = 1 but H^2_ét(P^1, Z/ℓ) ≅ Z/ℓ for ℓ invertible. Since the degree-1 comparison H^1(π_1, F) ≅ H^1_ét(X, F) holds for every connected X, a definition testing only i ≤ 1 wrongly accepts P^1.
Over a field of characteristic 0, a connected smooth curve that is affine or has genus ≥ 1 is an étale K(π,1) (SCHMIDT-STIX-16 Lemma 2.7(1)).

Over a field of characteristic 0, strongly hyperbolic Artin neighbourhoods (towers of elementary fibrations in hyperbolic curves), e.g. M_{0,n} for n ≥ 4, are K(π,1) (SCHMIDT-STIX-16 Proposition 2.8 and Definition 6.1).
Over a field of characteristic 0, a product of geometrically connected, geometrically unibranch K(π,1) varieties is a K(π,1) (SCHMIDT-STIX-16 Lemma 2.7(2)).

For all finite coefficients, the definition is equivalent to π_n^ét(X, x̄) = 0 for n ≥ 2, i.e. the classifying map X_et → Bπ_1 is an isomorphism in Ho(pro-ss_*) (Artin–Mazur 4.3); the full version implies the p-power-coefficient version of FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24.

definitions.name: Pushouts of schemes along closed immersions (pinching, conductor squares)
definitions.define: Given a closed immersion Z → Y and a finite morphism Z → Z', the pushout Y' = Y ⊔_Z Z' is a scheme (or algebraic space) with a finite map Y → Y', a closed immersion Z' → Y', and O_{Y'} = O_Y ×_{O_Z} O_{Z'} (a geometric pushout in WITASZEK-22's sense); affinely Spec(B ×_{B/I} A'). Conductor squares of finite birational maps, and pinching a closed subscheme to a finite quotient of it, are instances.

library.missing: Mathlib has pushouts of schemes only along open immersions (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Limits.lean, the HasPushout instance for two open immersions); no pushout along a closed immersion and a finite map, no conductor square and no geometric-pushout predicate.

api.statement: Gluing the points t = ±1 of A^1_k (char k ≠ 2) gives the nodal cubic: k + (t^2 − 1)k[t] = k[t^2 − 1, t(t^2 − 1)] = {f ∈ k[t] : f(1) = f(−1)}.
Pinching the double point V(t^2) ⊂ A^1 to Spec k gives the cusp: k[t] ×_{k[t]/(t^2)} k = k + t^2k[t] = k[t^2, t^3].

A topological pushout need not be geometric: A^1 → Spec k[t^2, t^5] with V(t^2) → Spec k is a commuting square of universal homeomorphisms, but k[t^2, t^5] ≠ k + t^2k[t] (it misses t^3), so it is not the pushout.

(Ferrand) For affine Y = Spec B, Z = Spec B/I and Z' = Spec A' with A' → B/I finite, Y' = Spec(B ×_{B/I} A') is the pushout in schemes, the square is also cartesian, Y → Y' is finite, and Y ∖ Z ≅ Y' ∖ Z'.
Formation of the pushout commutes with flat base change on Y': (B ×_{B/I} A') ⊗ F ≅ (B ⊗ F) ×_{(B/I) ⊗ F} (A' ⊗ F) for flat F.
For a separable quadratic extension E/k, pinching Spec E ⊂ P^1_k to Spec k gives a rational nodal curve with non-split node (SCHROER-23/170, type I_1 non-split).

definitions.name: Hilbert–Samuel function and multiplicity of a local ring or module
definitions.define: For a Noetherian local ring (A, m), an m-primary ideal q and a finitely generated A-module M, n ↦ ℓ_A(M/q^{n+1}M) agrees for n ≫ 0 with a polynomial of degree d = dim M. The multiplicity e(q; M) is d! times its leading coefficient, and e(M) = e(m; M). Pin the convention: IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 uses e_A(M) normalised by d = dim A, so that it vanishes when dim M < dim A; record both. For a point x of a curve, mult_x C = e(O_{C,x}).

library.missing: Mathlib's Polynomial.hilbertPoly is the Hilbert polynomial attached to a rational power series p/(1 − X)^d. Neither pin has the Hilbert–Samuel function of a module over a local ring, its eventual polynomiality, or the multiplicity e(q; M); grep for Hilbert–Samuel/Samuel multiplicity in both trees finds nothing.

api.statement: For a reduced plane curve singularity A = k[[x,y]]/(f), e(A) = ord(f): 1 at a smooth point, 2 for the node y^2 − x^2(x+1) and for the cusp y^2 − x^3, 3 for x^3 − y^3.
For finitely generated M over Noetherian local (A, m), ℓ(M/m^{n+1}M) is a polynomial in n of degree dim M for n ≫ 0, so e(M) is a positive integer when M ≠ 0.
A regular local ring has e(A) = 1; conversely (Nagata), a formally equidimensional (unmixed) local ring with e(A) = 1 is regular.

A = k[[x,y]]/(xy, y^2) has ℓ(A/m^{n+1}) = n + 2 for n ≥ 1, so e(A) = 1, but A is not regular (embedding dimension 2 > dim A = 1, embedded prime): the unmixedness hypothesis in Nagata's criterion is needed.

Associativity: e(q; M) = Σ_p ℓ(M_p) e(q; A/p) over primes p with dim A/p = dim M; hence e is additive on short exact sequences of modules of the same dimension (the fact IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 uses).
For a parameter ideal q of A, e(q; A) ≤ ℓ(A/q), with equality iff A is Cohen–Macaulay (Serre); and e(A) = e(A^) for the m-adic completion.
